title: A quasi-finite cover of affine n-space has dimension at most n
statement: Let $k$ be a field, an integer $n\ge0$, and $T$ a commutative $k$-algebra of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Suppose there is a $k$-algebra homomorphism $k[t_1,\dots,t_n]\to T$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] which is quasi-finite: it is of finite type and quasi-finite at every prime of $T$ in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime]. Then the Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] of $\operatorname{Spec}T$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is at most $n$ (including the empty spectrum, whose dimension is $-\infty$).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00QG (lemma-dimension-quasi-finite-over-polynomial-algebra, lines 31291-31305), via Tag 00QF (lemma-dimension-inequality-quasi-finite) and Tag 00OP (lemma-dim-affine-space)

proof.text: Put P = k[t_1, ..., t_n]. Mathlib's MvPolynomial.ringKrullDim_of_isNoetherianRing gives dim P = dim k + n = n: rewrite the field dimension using ringKrullDimZero_iff_ringKrullDim_eq_zero and simplify Nat.card_fin. This is a three-line specialization of the Noetherian polynomial dimension theorem (Mathlib/RingTheory/KrullDimension/Polynomial.lean:120-136), using the zero-dimensional field instance and Mathlib/RingTheory/KrullDimension/Zero.lean:62-67.

source.place: Tag 00QG, proof, first sentence: bound the local dimensions of the polynomial source; implemented by the global polynomial dimension calculation in Mathlib rather than the maximal-localization detour through 00OP

proof.text: Let q be a prime of T and p its contraction to P under the algebra structure induced by the given map. Install that algebra structure and its supplied finite-type instance. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-inequality-quasi-finite] with the supplied quasi-finiteness at q. Rewrite dim T_q and dim P_p as heights with [lem-weil-pbc-localization-dimension-chains-below-prime]. The height of p is at most dim P (Ideal.height_le_ringKrullDim_of_isPrime, Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Height.lean:167-170), which is n by step 1. Thus ht(q) <= n.

source.place: Tag 00QG, proof, application of 00QF; height bounded by global dimension is the immediate inclusion of chains below p among all prime chains

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-spec-topological-krull-dimension-ring] to replace the topological dimension of Spec T with dim T. The supremum-of-heights identity [lem-pc-ring-dimension-supremum-heights], in the inequality form ringKrullDim_le_iff_height_le (Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Height.lean:364-372), reduces the conclusion to ht(q) <= n for every prime q; step 2 supplies this. The identity and criterion also hold for the zero ring, whose empty spectrum has bottom dimension.

source.place: Tag 00QG, proof, final conclusion; expanded with Tags 00KG (dimension as supremum of heights) and 00KE/00ES (topological dimension equals ring dimension)
